failure_cause_assessments.reason: Product cause: recomputed samples are opaque #CFCDC5 instead of the approved #AAA99F in a solid glyph-free strip inside the uniquely resolved workshop.submit semantic box, fully within the native viewport. The original PNG shows the dimmed actual disabled primary button, not outer host background or an overlaid child. The submitted component applies PlainButtonStyle() and .disabled(selected == nil) to its own painted label; its palette declares the approved disabled color but the rendered button has the default disabled dimming. The approved bridge only decodes the model/maps callbacks and does not repaint the button. Enabled states render the intended enabled fill. The likely mechanism is default button-style disabled opacity; exact internal SwiftUI compositing is inferred, while component ownership and the rendered mismatch are directly evidenced.
